title: Acaranga Sutra
author: mahavira
attributionNote: Traditionally preserves the teaching of Mahāvīra as transmitted by his disciple Sudharman, in whose voice the lectures are spoken. The text reached its present form through a long process of transmission and canon formation.
description: The first and oldest of the Śvetāmbara canon's twelve Aṅgas, in two books: eight lectures on the discipline of the mendicant and the harm done by the passions, and sixteen on the begging of food, drink, clothes and a couch, the postures of the ascetic and the rules of conduct. Its first lecture, 'Knowledge of the Weapon', examines the causes of injury, and the whole work is the classical statement of ahiṃsā as a daily discipline.
historicalContext: The Śvetāmbara canon was fixed at the council of Valabhī in the fifth century CE, drawing on older oral tradition. The Acaranga is the oldest layer of that canon and the standard source for the early Jain ascetic ethic; its attention to life in earth, water, fire and plants has made it central to modern Jain identity and to environmental readings of Jainism.
availabilityNote: Streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive view by view at read time. Jacobi's 1884 translation is public domain; the Prakrit text is not included.

editions.attributionText: Jaina Sutras, Part I (Sacred Books of the East, vol. 22), translated by Hermann Jacobi (1884). Public domain in the United States. Read from the Internet Sacred Text Archive, sacred-texts.com.

editions.notes: Jacobi's 1884 translation for the Sacred Books of the East, with his introduction. The printed page numbers the scan carried in the text are dropped and the paragraphs a page turn cut in two are rejoined; Jacobi's footnotes are the volume's apparatus and are not carried. The verse numbers he prints in parentheses are kept.
